request: Systematically review all remaining uncertainty-marked scientific-name explanations against sources, correcting German, English and Dutch as needed.
method: Enumerate every uncertainty-marked runtime term and subtract the cases actually covered by the previous content sample. Do not use the broad depth-rewrite record as proof of an individual content check.
Read the actual source entry, including page continuations, and compare historical combinations, word components, proposed motives and competing interpretations.

Prefer an attested historical transmission over an attractive but undocumented decomposition. Retain conjectures as conjectures, and distinguish an unidentified ancient bird from an unknown word origin.
Check all three language versions together and compile the explicit source/page/scope assignments. Use a species-specific override when the same epithet has different histories.

cases.finding: The historical species name Loxia astrild is documented; a German/Dutch avicultural origin is proposed, not established. Explain this path without assigning an unverified original language.

Two consulted bird-name dictionaries assign different persons to the kingfisher epithet. Show the disagreement with attribution and retain uncertainty; do not import the hummingbird genus Atthis explanation as settled evidence.

Separate two taxon-specific uses. For Panurus, Biarmia/Bjarmaland and a possible reshaping of Beardmanica compete. For Falco, Jobling interprets Temminck’s reuse as referring to the moustachial markings. Neither supplies a secure geographical origin for the falcon.

The Italian Hazel Grouse name Bonasia is attested; comparison with Greek bonasos/Latin bonasus (wild ox) is a proposal, not a resolved decomposition. No speculative roast-based folk etymology is asserted.
Distinguish the documented pre-Linnaean name Canuti avis and Latin Canutus from unverified stories explaining its connection with the king. Jobling also records an onomatopoeic proposal.
Harcourt’s adoption of Roque de Castro/Crasto is documented in the reference. Literal and onomatopoeic interpretations are proposals; retain uncertainty about the local name’s deeper origin.
Greek kollourion is documented; its identification with a particular shrike or thrush is conjectural. Remove repetitive prose while keeping the unresolved identification and deeper origin distinct.

The dedication to the Glasgow physician who supplied a specimen and description is supported. Jobling records competing Peter/Patrick identifications; the BOU does not resolve the first name. Clarify that the dedication itself is not what is uncertain.

Jobling supports a probable relation to the botanical name Githago. Do not turn a proposed plant comparison or a particular colour motive into an established naming intention. Replace the unavailable WNVE main citation with the consulted reference.

Re-read Kollibay’s short original article: it introduces a replacement for a preoccupied name and discusses Ogilvie-Grant’s work, but gives no explicit dedication. Add that context and printed page; retain the qualified inference.

Jobling says the etymology is undiscovered and offers only broad Indian-name/mythology guesses without an attested source word. The existing concise statement of uncertainty is appropriate and is retained unchanged.
Jobling records no explanation by Linnaeus. Present the melas/melanos plus albus contraction explicitly as a proposal; fitting the plumage is not proof of actual formation.
Separate the menstrual sense selected by Jobling from the lexical base mensis (month), independently checked in Lewis & Short. Neither the month base nor plumage colour establishes the naming motive.

Jobling and Mouchard support the ancient eagle-name reading from plangos. The separately attested flat-footed sense does not prove Miller’s intention. Make the source-supported analysis explicit while retaining the limit.

Italian rail-name forms are documented. Jobling’s Venetian localisation differs from Mouchard’s Po-valley proposal; BOU calls the derivation unknown. Explain that shared Italian provenance is firmer than the regional or deeper etymology.
Keep Medieval Latin qualea as a proposal, not a certain source word. The reason for applying a quail name to a weaverbird is unresolved, and Jobling also records an African-name proposal.
Read the entry across both printed pages. Include the competing Quisqueya and Medieval Latin bird-name hypotheses rather than presenting only the Indigenous-name proposal; neither is settled.

Sonnerat’s French Rouloul de Malacca is documented; the proposed Malay Roulroul is not verified in the dictionaries checked by Jobling. Separate that secure transmission from the unconfirmed deeper language claim.

Jobling’s rubus/bramble account is corroborated by Vorobyev’s identification of Gaza’s rendering of Greek batis from batos. Remove the generic uncertainty flag for word formation; historical disagreement about whinchat/stonechat identity is stated separately. BOU 1915:99 is older and tentative; it is not used to override the documented translation history.

The ordinary/common sense and the base trivium (crossroads) are secure. BOU interprets the epithet as common; a deliberate reference to roadside habitat is not documented by these sources. Replace the unavailable WNVE main reference and qualify the habitat inference.
The link to the earlier Loxia astrild is documented; add that historical combination. The German/Dutch avicultural origin of astrild remains proposed.
The naming authors gave no explanation according to Jobling. Attribute the idoneus comparison explicitly as a conjecture rather than asserting a classical or mythological derivation.

Read Coues’s original discussion and Mouchard’s Swainson quotation. The intended uninvited guest is documented; molos/throsko and molobros are competing analyses, not an unqualified literal decomposition.
Add the historical route through Rallus porzana and attested Italian forms. Preserve the unresolved regional/deeper origin rather than making the entire borrowing uncertain.
The route through Emberiza quelea is documented. Distinguish that certain historical link from the proposed qualea root and unverified transfer motive.
The route through Gracula quiscula is documented. Add both main deeper-origin proposals from the entry’s continuation, without choosing between them.
Add the route through Phasianus rouloul and Sonnerat’s French name. Do not label the ultimate word as securely Malay.

Duméril’s French Surnie and its use for long-tailed owls are documented. Jobling and BOU do not support a secure Greek root; avoid turning dictionary speculation into a fact. Printed BOU page is 132, not the nearby older-reference page 129.
Edwards’s English Touraco is documented. Its supposed West African origin does not identify a verified source language or word meaning; state that limit.
Leach’s Xeme/Xema is documented. Jobling and BOU treat it as probably invented; proposed Greek associations do not establish a meaning.
Retain the cautious Porzana reshaping. Jobling calls it an anagram, but direct letter comparison shows an extra i. Make that disagreement explicit without inventing a reason for the added letter.

Full article retrieved through web tool; its cautious identification matches the Jobling entry
Full Lewis & Short entry as rendered at Gadsden Classics; used only for word component, not bird naming motive

limitations: All 31 remaining marked terms were reviewed; the total catalogue of unmarked terms was not systematically audited in this pass.

Not every naming author’s original publication was retrievable. Findings based on dictionaries are identified as such; retained uncertainty is not a claim that every original source has been exhausted.

WNVE pages for atthis, githagineus and trivialis were unavailable. Their main references were replaced with consulted sources, and contradictory lexicon interpretations of atthis are stated explicitly.

The Montagu original-description download timed out; dougallii was checked in Jobling and BOU instead. The subsequently announced 1910 congress contribution on granti was sought but not obtained; the short 1910 original paper was re-read.
Wember (2005) remains bibliographic further reading only; its full text was not consulted.
This report is a content audit. Tests verify coverage, source assignment, taxon-specific routing and rendering; they do not independently establish linguistic truth.
